Rapid treatment of overdosage with naloxone and as- sisted respiration is essential. Cardiac effects may not be reversed by naloxone. Gastric lavage and activated charcoal may be of value within 1 hour of ingestion, but dialysis is of little use. Convulsions may require control with an anticonvul- sant, bearing in mind that the CNS depressant effects of dextropropoxyphene can be exacerbated (see also In- teractions, below). Stimulants should not be used be- cause of the risk of inducing convulsions. Patients taking overdoses of dextropropoxyphene with paracetamol will also require treatment for paraceta- mol poisoning (p.108).
